CHURCHILL, RIGHT HON. WINSTON LEONARD SPENCER, P.C. (1907).—M.P. for Oldham, 1900-6; for N.W. Manchester, 1906-8; for Dundee, 1908; late lieut. 4th Queen's Own Hussars; ed. Harrow, Sandhurst; entd. army, 1895; served with Spanish forces in Cuba, 1896 (1st cls. (Spanish) Order of Military Merit); served, attached 31st Punjab Infantry, with Malakand field force, 1897; present at operations in Bajaur, including actions of 16th and 30th Sept. (deepa. medal with clasp); served as orderly offr. to Sir W. Lockhart with Tirah exped. force, 1898 (clasp); served, attached 21st Lancers, with Nile exped. force, 1898; present at battle of Khartoum (medal with clasp); contested Oldham (C.) 1899; served as lieut. South Africa Light Horse; acted as correspdt., "Morning Post," South Africa, 1899-1900; taken prisoner, action 15th Nov., but escaped 12th Dec.; present at actions of Acton Homes, Venter's Spruit, Hussar Hill, Cingolo, Monte Cristo, and at battles of Spion Kop, Vaal Krantz, and Pieters; also operations round De-wetdorp, April, 1900; passage of Sand River, 15th May; engagements of Johannesburg and Diamond Hill, and capture of Pretoria (medal with six clasps); parly. under-sec. of state for the Colonies, Dec., 1905; visited Uganda and E. Africa, 1907; pres. of Bd. of T., 1908; Homese., 1910-11; first lord of the Admiralty, 1911; chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, 1915; min. of munitions, 1917; sec. of state, War Office and Air Ministry, Jan., 1919; S. of S. for the Colonies, 14th Feb., 1921 to 25th Oct., 1922; chancellor of the exchequer, 7th Nov., 1924; author of "The Story of the Malakand Field Force"; "The River War"; "Savrola"; "London to Ladysmith, via Pretoria"; "Ian Hamilton's March"; "Life of Lord Randolph Churchill."

CLARK, ADRIAN JOHN, LL.B. (Lond.), O.B.E. CLELAND, EDWARD ERskINE, K.C., LL.B.—B. 1869; ed. Prince Alfred Coll. and Adelaide Univ.; barrister-at-law; judge, sup.ct., Adelaide, 1936.

CLELAND, JOHN STOCKWIN, M.B.E., F.R.I.B.A., M.I.A.—Draughtsman, P.W.D., Transvaal, Mar., 1909; asst. archt., P.W.D., Union of S. Africa, Apr., 1912; archt., Sept., 1920; sec. for pub. wks., June, 1932.

CLEMENTI, Sir Cecil, G.C.M.G. (1931), K.C.M.G. (1926), C.M.G. (1916)—Ed. St. Paul's schl. and Magdalen Coll., Oxford (demv. 1894; B.A., 1898; M.A., 1901), hon. mention Hertford schl., 1895; 1st cl. mods., 1896; hon. mention Ireland and Craven schl., 1896; Boden Sanskrit scholar, 1897; prox. acc. Gaisford (Greek Prose), 1897; 2nd cl. lit. hum., 1898; prox. acc. Chancellor's Latin essay, 1899; cadet, Hong Kong, 1899; passed cadet, 1900; ag. asst. col. sec., and ag. elk. of councils, Dec., 1900, to Oct., 1901; asst. registr.-gen., Aug., 1901; mem. bd. of examrs. in Chinese, Apr., 1902; seconded for spec. serv. under govt. of India, May, 1902; J.P., June, 1902; ag. asst. col. sec., and elk. of councils, Sept., 1902, to June, 1903; sec. interpretation bd., Dec., 1902; seconded for famine relief work in Kwang Si, April to June, 1903; mem. of land ct., New Territories, Dec., 1903; ag. asst. land offr. and pol. mag., New Territories, May, 1905, to Sept., 1906; asst. col. sec. and elk. of councils, Oct., 1907; attended Internat. Opium Conf. at Shanghai, Feb., 1909; priv. sec. to H.E. the Admtr., Apr., 1910; ag. col. sec., and mem. exec. and legis. couns., on various occasions, 1911-12; col. sec., B. Guiana, 1913; admtd. govt., 8th June, 1916 to 14th Apr., 1917, Apr. to Oct., 1919 and June to Oct., 1921; col. sec., Ceylon, Nov., 1922; admtd. govt., Nov., 1922 to Feb., 1923 and Apr. to Oct., 1925; gov., Hong Kong, 1st Nov. 1925; kn. of Grace of St. John of Jerusalem, 1926; hon. L.L.D., Hong Kong Univ., 1926; gov. and commdr-in-ch., Straits Stltnts. and high comsnr., Malay States, 1929; resigned, 1934.

CLEMENTI, LOCKHART.—B. 1881; served in Cape Mounted Rifles; sub.-inspr., Basutoland Mounted Pol., 1905; inspr., 1913; served in European War; staff offr., 1926; dep. asst. comsnr., 1929; asst. comsnr., 1930; title changed to dist. comsnr., 1936.

CLEMENTS, JOHN BURTON, B.Sc. Forestry (Edin.)—B. 1891; for. offr., Nyasaland, Sept., 1920; ag. ch. for. offr., Oct. to Dec., 1920 and May to Dec., 1923; ch. for. offr., Dec., 1923.

CLEMMAY, A.V., M.A., M.B., B.Ch. (Oxf.), M.R.C.S., L.R.C.P., M.M.S.A.—B. 1901; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, July, 1928.

CLIFFORD, CAPT. HON. SIR BEDE EDMUND HUGH, K.C.M.G. (1933), C.B. (1931), C.M.G. (1924), M.V.O. (1920).—B. 1890; served, European War; pvt. sec. Lord Novar, gov.-gen. C wealth Australia, 1918-20; sec. H.R.H. Prince Arthur of Connaught (gov.-gen. and commdr.-in-ch., Union of S. Africa) 1921-23; sec. Earl of Athlone, gov.-gen and commander-in-ch., Union of S. Africa, 1924; Imp. sec., S. African high comsnr., Apr., 1924; rep. of H.M. Govt. of Gr. Britain in the Union of S. Africa, 1928; gov. and commdr.-in-ch. of the Bahamas, 1931; do., Mauritius, Oct., 1937.

CLIFFORD, GEOFFREY MILES.—B. 1897; ed. Heath Schl., Horsmonden, Kent; mily. serv., France and Flanders, 1915-18; army of the Rhine, 1919-20; admstve. offr., cls. IV, Nigeria, 1921; cls. III, 1929; dipl., anthropology, London Univ., 1933; ag. res., 1934 and 1935-37; admstve. offr., cls. II, 1937; ag. prin. asst. sec., secret., 1938.

CLIFFORD, SIR HUGH CHARLES, G.C.M.G. (1921), G.B.E., (1925), K.C.M.G. (1909); C.M.G. (1900).—B. 1866; joined Perak service, 1883; passed in Malay, Feb., 1885; collr. land rev., Kuala Kangsar, Mar., 1885; on special service to Palang, 1887 (recd. thanks of S. of S.); ag. govt. agt. there, 1887-8; supr., Ulu Pahang, 1889; ag. Br. res. Pahang, 1890 to 1891, and from Feb., 1893; took a leading part in suppression of Pahang rebellion, 1892; sec. to govt., Selangor, Dec., 1894, but continued to act as res. of Pahang; visited Cocos-Keeling Is. as special comsnr., June, 1894; led armed exped. into native states of Tréngganu and Kelantan to effect capture of fugitive rebel leaders, Mar.-June, 1895 (recd. thanks S. of S.); res., Pahang, July, 1896; gov. of North Borneo and Labuan, 1899 to 1901; Br. res., Pahang, 1901; ag. col. sec., Trinidad and Tobago, Sept., 1903, confirmed, Sept., 1904; sent on deputation to B. Guiana in Nov., 1905, to inquire into municipal institutions; admtd. govt., Mar. to Aug., 1904, and from Apr. to Oct., 1906; col. sec., Ceylon, May, 1907; admtd. govt., on various occasions, 1907-12; gov., G. Coast, Dec., 1912; gov., Nigeria, July, 1919; gov. of Ceylon, Nov., 1925; gov. S. Stltnts. and high comsnr., Malay
States, June, 1927; ret., 1929; concluded with M. Noufflard, the lieutenant-governor of Dahomey, in Aug., 1914 an agreement for the temporary partition between the British and French Goyta, and for the provisional administration of Togoland; admstd. Br. sphere of occupation from Aug., 1914, to Aug., 1919; chmn., comtes. on W. African trade and taxation, Oct.-Nov., 1921 (received thanks of S. of S.); is part author, with Sir Frank Swettenham, of a Malayan dictionary, and author of more than a dozen books, mostly on Malayan subjects, and of a translation of the penal code into Malay; also of a history of the G. Coast regt., in the E. African campaign.

CLIFF, ALBERT HALL.—B. 1898; ed. Boston G.S. & Keble Coll., Oxford; final exam. B.A. (rural econ.) 1923; served with H.M. forces, Italy, 1917-18; supt., educn., Nigeria, 1924; prin., King's Coll., Lagos, 1936.

CLIPSHAM, PHILIP RICHARD.—B. 1903; apptd. after compet. exam., cler. offr., C.O., 30th Sept., 1920; seconded as regar. on staff of high commnr., in Canada for H.M.'s govt. in Gt. Britain, 1932; rtd. to C.O. as cler. offr., higher grade, 4th Dec., 1937.

CLIVE, CAPT. J. H.—Asst. dist. commnr., Kenya, May., 1920; dist. offr., 1923.

CLOETE, PHILIP ALBERT (B.Sc., Cape).—B. 1842; ed. S.A. Coll., Cape Town, S.A., Schl. of Mines, Kimberley and Johannesburg; B.E.F., France, S.A. Heavy Arty., 1917-18; asst. inspr., mines, 1927; asst. gen. man., state alluvial mines, Namaqualand, 1929; inspr., mining leases, Union of S.A., 1934.

CLOSE, R. W., B.A., LL.B., K.C.—B. 1867; ed. S. African Coll., Cape Town; M.P. for Rondebosch, 1920-29; Mowbray, 1929-33; leader, Cape bar; min. plenip., Washington, Jan., 1934.

CLUBB, HON. WILLIAM REID.—B. 1884; served on Morris munici. coun., 1916-20; mem., leg. assembly for Morris, Manitoba, 1920-22; re-elec., July, 1922; min. of public works, Manitoba, 8th Aug., 1922; re-elec. for Morris by accl., 26th Aug., 1922.

CLURK, REGINALD MONTAGU.—B. 1891; ed. Clifton Coll. and Balliol Coll., Oxford; B.A. (hons. schl., jurisprudence); barrister-at-law, Inner Temple, 1915; served Great War, 1914-15; res. mag., Jamaica, Mar., 1932; crown coun., S. Stlntte, 1937.

CLUTTERBUCK, P.A., M.C.—B. 1897; schol. of Malvern Coll. and of Pembroke Coll., Cambridge, 1915; Coldstream Guards, 1916-19; capt. and adjt., 3rd batt., Oct., 1917; M.C. and ment. in desps., 1918; apptd. under reconstruction scheme, asst. prin., G.P.O., 1st Sept., 1919; transfd. to C.O., 13th Feb., 1922; sec., managing comtee, Imperial Bureau of Mycology, 1923-25; addnl. pte. sec. to parly. under sec. (Lord Arnold), June-Oct., 1924; sec., Milner-Lovat agrl. comtee., 1924-25; sec., Donoughmore coman. on Ceylon constitution and visited Ceylon, 1927-28; pte. sec. to perm. under sec. for Doms. affrs., 23rd Aug., 1928; prin., Doms. Office, 14th Nov., 1929; U.K. delegn. to L. of N. assembly, 1929, 1930 and 1931; negotiations with Egypt, 1930; reparations conferees., Lond., 1931 and Lausanne, 1933; sec., Newfoundland Royal Coman. and visited Newfoundland (twice) and Canada, 1933; further visit to Newfoundland, Sept.-Oct., 1938.

CLUVER, COL. EUSTRACE HENRY, M.A., M.D., B.Ch., D.P.H.—B. 1894; ed. at Victoria Coll., Stellenbosch, S. Africa, Hartford Coll., Oxford and King's Coll. Hosp., London; Rhodes schol. for Stellenbosch; Burrey Yeo. schol., King's Coll.; senr. demy, Magdalen Coll., Oxford; 1st cls., final hons., nat. science (physiology); served with 1st S. African field ambulance in France; lecturer in geology, Victoria Coll., Stellenbosch, 1914; prof. of physiology, Univ. of Witwatersrand, Johannesburg, 1919-26; asst. health offr., Union of S. Africa, 1926; senr. asst. health offr., do., 1934; dep. ch. health offr., Union S. Africa, 1937; transfd. E. of O., with rank of maj., S.A.M.C., 1929; lieut.-col., R. of O., 1932; D.D.M.S. defence headqrs., 1933; D.M.S. with temp. rank of col., 1934; comdr., Order of Hosp. of St. John of Jerusalem, 1935; col., 1937; assoc. edr., Journal of Industrial Hygiene (America); published many papers in tech. jnl.s. on subject of physiology and hygiene.

CLUVER, FREDERICK WILLIAM PAUL, B.A. (Cape), M.B., Ch.B. (Edin.), D.P.H. (Cape Town). Fellow of the Royal Institute of Public Health; major, S.A.M.C. (res. of offrs.).—Ed. Victoria Coll., Stellenbosch, Edinburgh Univ. and Univ. of Cape Town; res. med. offr., gen. hosp., Pretoria, and med. offr., to S.A. Air Force (major S.A.M.C.), 1924; O.C., mily. hosp., Wynberg, 1926; O.C., mily. hosp., Roberts Heights, 1927; asst. health offr., Union health dept., Pretoria, 1932; do., Durban, 1933.

COAKER, HON. SIR WM. F., K.B.E. (1923).—President, fisherman's protective union, Newfoundland; M.H.A. for Bonavista, 1913; M.H.A., Twillingate, 1914; mem. of tonnage comtee., 1917; M.E.C., 1917; min. without portfolio, 1918.

COALES, FRANCIS GEORGE, M.I.C.E., M.I.S.E.—B. 1889; ed. D.P.W., 1925; exec. engr., in ch. deptl. tech. schl., 1925-27; 2nd lieut., M.S.V.R., 1926; lieut., M.S.V.R., 1929; senr. exec. engr., Jan., 1930; state engr., grade II, Jan., 1936; grade I, Sept., 1936; ag. dep. D.P.W., S.S., Apr., 1937.

COATES, RT. HON. JOSEPH GORDON, P.C. (1926). M.C.—B. 1878; ed. privately; mem. of New Zealand parl. since 1911; min. of justice, 1919-20; P.M.G., 1919-25; min. of pub. wks., 1920-26; min., native affrs., 1921-1928; min. rly., 1923-1928; prime min., 1925-1928; min., external affrs., 1928; min., mines, 1928; min., agr., 1928; ret. from office, 1928; joined coalition miny., 1931; min., pub. wks., 1931-33; min., transport, 1931-35; min., finance, 1933-35; min., cust., 1933-35; N.Z. rep. at Imp. Conf., 1926 and at Ottawa conf., 1932; served with N.Z. Exped. Force as capt. and major, 1916-1919; awarded M.C. with bar.

COATS, ROBERT HAMILTON, B.A., F.S.S. (hon.), F.R.C.S.—B. 1874; ed. Toronto Univ.; bankers scholarship in polit. economy, and Wyld prize, English; on staff of "Toronto Globe," 1897-1900; editor, Labour Gaz., and ch. statistician, dept. of labour, 1901-12; mem., coman. on the cost of living, 1913-14; dom. statistician and contr. of census, 1914; author of "The Labour Movement in Canada" (Canada and its Provinces); joint author of life of James Douglas (Makers of Canada series); offl. del. to Br. Empire Statistical Conference, 1920; mem. of coman. on statistics under the League of Nations, 1920; mem., International Statistical Inst.

COBB, FREDERIC.—B. 1885; ed. Charterhouse and Worcester Coll., Oxford; B.A. (Oxon.); European mast., F.M.S., Sept., 1921; headmast., King George V Sch., Seremban, May, 1934; Eur.
CHRISTOFFELSZ, ARTHUR ERIC, B.A., LL.B., Cantab., barrister-at-law (Grays Inn).—B. 1890; cadet, local div., Ceylon civ. serv., Mar., 1915; extra office asst., Jaffna kach., and pol. mag., Jaffna, Jan., 1917; office asst., Badulla kach., Mar., 1919; pol. mag., Dandagamuwa, Oct., 1920; ditto, Kurunegala, Sept., 1921; asst. attimt. offr., Oct., 1926; asst. attimt. offr., Dec., 1927; asst. govt. agt., Kegalla, June, 1931; do., Putalam and Chilaw, Sept., 1933; ag. govt. agt., N.W.P., Mar., 1937.

CHURCH, BASIL HAMPDEN, M.C.—B. 1890; asst. govt. marine surv., Hongkong, 1927.

CHURCHILL, WILLIAM FOSTER NORTON.—B. 1898; ed. Cheltenham Coll. and Sidney Sussex Coll.; Camb. CHURCHILL, RIGHT HON. WINSTON LEONARD SPENCER, P.C. (1907).—M.P. for Oldham, 1900-6; for N.W. Manchester, 1906-8; for Dundee, 1908; late lieut. 4th Queen's Own Hussars; ed. Harrow, Sandhurst; entd. army, 1896; served with Spanish forces in Cuba, 1896 (lst cls. (Spanish) Order of Military Merit); served, attached 31st Punjab Infantry, with Malakand field force, 1897; present at operations in Bajaur, including actions of 16th and 30th Sept. (desp. medal with clasp); served as orderly offr. to Sir W. Lockhart with Tirah exped. force, 1898 (clasp); served, attached 21st Lancers, with Nile exped. force, 1898; present at battle of Khartoum (medal with clasp); contested Oldham (C.) 1899; served as lieut. South Africa Light Horse; acted as correspdt., "Morning Post," South Africa, 1899-1900; taken prisoner, action 15th Nov., but escaped 12th Dec.; present at actions of Acton Homes, Venter's Spruit, Hussar Hill, Cingolo, Monte Cristo, and at battles of Spion Kop, Vaal Krantz, and Pieters; also operations round De-wetshoep, April, 1900; passage of Sand River, 15th May; engagements of Johannesburg and Diamond Hill, and capture of Pretoria (medal with six clasps); parly. under-sec. of state for the Colonies, Dec. 1905; visited Uganda and E. Africa, 1907; pres. of Bd. of T., 1908; Homeseo, 1910-11; first lord of the Admiralty, 1911; chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, 1915; min. of munitions, 1917; sec. of state, War Office and Air Ministry, Jan., 1919; S. of S. for the Colonies, 14th Feb., 1921 to 25th Oct., 1922; chancellor of the exchequer, 7th Nov., 1924; author of "The Story of the Malakand Field Force"; "The River War"; "Savrola"; "London to Ladysmith, via Pretoria"; "Ian Hamilton's March"; "Life of Lord Randolph Churchill."

CILLIERS, CHARL. ANDRIES, B.A.—B. 1893; ed. Victoria Coll., Stellenbosch (now Univ. of Stellenbosch); clk., defence dept., Union of S.A., 1913; pvt. sec. to min. of lands, 1916; ditto, to min. of defence, 1917; ditto, to min. of agr., 1921; under-sec. for pub. wks., 1934.

CLAIRMONTE, FREDERICK ARCHIBALD CONRAD.—B. 1886; ed. Harrison Coll., Codrington Coll., and Ontario Business Coll.; ent. civ. serv., Barbados, 1909; war serv., 1916-19; clk., pol. mag., cts., dist. "A," 1927; ag. pol. mag., various dists., on several occasions, 1928-31; comm., income tax, 1935.

CLARENDON, EARL OF (of 1776) Rt. Hon. GEORGE HERBERT HYDE VILLEERS, P.C. (1931), G.C.M.G. (1930), J.P., D.L.—B. 1877; ed. Eton; priv. lord-in-waiting to H.M.; hon. lieut.-col. (Hertford Regt.) A.D.C. to Lord Lieut. of Ireland (Lord Dudley); chanc., Primrose League, 1919-21; capt., Gentlemen-at-Arms, 1922-23 and 1924-25; dep. speaker, House of Lords; parly. under-sec. of state for dominion affrs., and chmn., overseas settlement cte., 9th July, 1925; chmn. B.B.C., 1927; gov. gen., Union of S. Africa, 1931-37.

CLARK, ADRIAN JOHN, LL.B. (Lond.). O.B.E. (Mily.)—B. 1889; King's schol. and Good-enough medallist (Fr. and German), Westminster; called to bar, Inner Temple, 1910; junr. coun. to treasy., 1917; served in Great War, France, 1915-19; capt., 23rd London Regt.; D.A.A.G., Third Army and lieut.-col., R.A.F., (S.O. 1st grade); brevet-major and twice ment. in despatches; mag., Victoria, Trinidad, July, 1924; ag. puisne judge, Sept. to Dec., 1924; P.O.S., Trinidad, Jan., 1927; puisne judge, Jamaica, May, 1927; ag. ch. just., July-Nov., 1932; dep. pub. pros., S'pore, Sept., 1934; puisne judge, S.S., 1936; legal advr., F.M.S., 1936.

CLARK, SIR ERNEST, K.C.B., K.C.M.G., C.B.E.—Ent. Br. civ. serv., 1884; called to bar, Middle Temple, 1894; Cavo Govt., 1904-05; asst. sec. to bd. of inland rev. and of R. commn. on income tax, 1919-20; asst. under-sec. for Ireland, sec. to treasy. and head of civ. serv. N. Ireland, 1920; mem., economic mission to Australia, 1928-29; and of other commns. and comtees, including the joint exchequer bd. of G. Br. and N. Ireland.

CLARK, ERNEST MALCOLM, M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), D.T.M. & H. (Lond.)—B. 1908; ed. St. Bartholomew's Hosp., Lond.; late senr. res. med. offr., West Suffolk Gen. Hosp.; med. offr., Somaliland, Nov., 1933; do., Kenya, 1937.

CLARK, JOHN BUCHANAN.—B. 1897; ed., George Watson's Coll., Edinburgh; S.A. Coll. Schls. and S.A. Coll. (now Univ. of Cape Town); Balliol Coll., Oxford; M.A. (Cape Town), B.A. (Hons.), Oxon.; Rhodes schol., 1917; 2nd lt. and lt., R.A.S.C., France, Aug., 1917 to Feb., 1919; lect. in hist., Univ. of Cape Town, 1921; lect., classics and hist., Univ. of Witwatersrand, 1924; inspr., schls., June, 1925; ag. dir., European educn., June, 1926-June, 1927; dir., European educn., N. Rhodesia, June, 1927; mem., European educn., comsn., N. Rhodesia, 1929; M.L.C. in 1930, 1931 and 1935; ag. dir. native educn., 1936; mem., educn. films bd. and comtes. on nutrition, 1936.

CLARK, JOHN ERNEST—B. 1883, crown solr., N.S.W., 1930.

CLARK, J. MOK., Ch.B. (Aberdeen), D.T.M. (Liverpool), Certif., Liverpool Schl. of Trop. Med.—Apptd. to W.A.M.S., Sierra Leone, 1914; served in Cameroons Expedy. Force, 1915-16; temp. lieut. (gen. list), 1915-16; temp. med. offr., E. Africa, 1916; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 19th Apr., 1918; senr. med. offr., Apr., 1924.

CLARK, RICHARD JOHN BOND, A.R.I.B.A. (shart. archt.)—B. 1896; ed. Cornwall County Schl.; archt., P.W.D., Hong Kong, 1924.
CLARK, WILLIAM CLIFFORD, C.M.G. (1935), M.A., LL.D.—B. 1889; ed. Williamstown High Schl., Queen's Univ. (Kingston) and Harvard Univ. (Ricardo prize scholarship, Harvard Univ., 1915); Henry Lee memorial fellow and tutor, divn. of hist., govt. and economics, Harvard Univ., 1914-15; successively lecturer, asst. prof., assoc. prof. and prof., economics, Queen's Univ., 1915-23; advr., dept. of lab., Ottawa, 1918-19; prof., commerce, etc., Queen's Univ., 1931-32; finan. advr., Imp. Economic Conf., Ottawa, 1932; dep. min., finance and sec. treas., bd., Ottawa, Nov., 1932; dep. min. of finance, 1936; off., advr., World Monetary and Economic Conf., 1933; author of various papers in economics and finance and collaborator in Warshaw's "Representative American Industries."

CLARK, SIR WILLIAM HENRY, G.C.M.G. (1937), K.C.S.I. (1915), K.C.M.G. (1930), C.S.I. (111), C.M.G. (1903).—B. 1876; Ed. Eton and Trinity Coll., Cambridge; clk. Bd. of T., 1899; sec. to sp. mission to Shanghai to negotiate comm'l. treaty with China, 1901; ag. 2nd sec., diplomatic serv., 1902; sec. to royal comm. on supply of food, etc., in time of war, 1903-5; pvt. sec. at Bd. of T. to Rt. Hon. D. Lloyd George, 1906, and to Rt. Hon. W. S. Churchill, 1908; and to Rt. Hon. D. Lloyd George as chancellor of the exchequer, 1908-10; mem. for commerce and industry of the coun. of the Viceroy of India, 1910-16; compt-r.-gen., comm'l. intell. dept. Bd. of T., 1916; compt-r.-gen. dept. of overseas trade, Sept., 1917; high comm'r for Great Britain in Canada, Sept., 1928; high comm'r for Basutoland, the Bechuanaland Prot. and Swaziland and high comm'r in the Union of S. CLARKE, ARTHUR GRENFELL, B.A.—B. 1906; ed. CLARKE, F. H.—Asst. game warden, R.A.P., 1919; ag. game warden, Kenya, 1932; senr. asst. do., 1937.

CLARKE, HON. SIR FRANCIS GRENVILLE, K.B.E., M.L.C.—B. 1879; ed. Scotch Coll., Melbourne, Melbourne Univ. and Exeter Coll., Oxford; M.L.C. for N. Prov. (Vic.); min. for lands and water supply, Nov., 1917 to Oct., 1919; min. of pub. wks. and water supply, Oct., 1919 to July, 1923; pres., leg. coun., Victoria, July, 1923.

CLARKE, HON. SIR FREDERICK JAMES, K.C.M.G. (1911), C.M.G. (1907).—Ed. Christ Church Med. Schl., Barbados, and Caius Coll., Cambridge; B.A., 1879; M.H.A., Barbados, 1887; pres., Barbados agric. soc'y, 1905; mem., cent. poor law board; M.E.C., 1905; J.P.; O.C., Barbados vol. force, 1906; speaker, H. of A., Barbados, 1898-1934.

CLARKE, FRANCIS PRIESTLEY COURTNEY.—B. 1879; ed. Halleyburry and Univ. Coll., Oxford; B.A., Oxford, 1901; LL.B., Cape, 1909; advoc., sup. et., Cape, 1910; ent. Cape civ. ser., 1903; served in depts. of justice, native affrs. and forests; ch. dlr., S.W.A. admstr., 1923; asst. sec., 1925; sec. for S.W.A., 1934; chmn., S.W.A.—Angola bndry., and Cunene Water comm., 1929; rep. States, June, 1927; ret., 1929; concluded with M. Noufflard, the lieut.-gov. of Dahomey, in Aug., 1914 an agreement for the temporary partition between the British and French Govts., and for the provisional administration of Togoland; admstd. COLLINS, COL. COMMDT. THE HON., WILLIAM RICHARD, D.T.D., D.S.O.—B. 1876; ed. COLLYMORE, ERNEST ALLAN, M.A. (Oxon.), K.C. (1933)—B. 1893; ed. COLTON, WILLIAM DOUGLAS.—B. 1900; ed. Cheltenham Coll.; treasy. elk. N. Rhodesia, Mar., 1927; ast. treas., Apr., 1930; ag. dep. treas., Sept., 1937; dep. ast. gen., Jan., 1938; ag. ast. gen., Jan., 1938.

COMBE, SIR RALPH MOLINEUX, KT. BACH. (1920). Ed. at Haileybury Coll. and Exeter Coll., Oxford; B.A., 1894; called to the bar, Inner Tem., 1897; Crown advocate, E. CONIBEAR, JAMES HANFORD.—Reg. army, 1897-1919; sub.-inpr., pol. and keeper, prisons, St. Lucia, Nov., 1920; ag. ch., pol. and impr. prisons, 1922; prison supt., Gold Coast, Jan., 1924; lieut., G.C. CONNELL, W. K., M.B., Ch.B. (Glas.), F.R.C.S. (Eng.), D.T.M. & H. (Lond.).—B. 1893; mily. serv., R.A.M.C., 1916-20; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, July, 1924; senr. surg. specialist, 1934.

CONNOLLY, HON. SIR JAMES DANIEL, KT. BACH. (1920).—B. 1870; ed. Warwick Pub. COOK, James, L.R.C.P. & S. (Edin.), L.R.F.P. & S. (Glas.), F.R.C.S. (Edin.), D.P.H., Durham—B. 1904; med. asst., col. hosp., Port of Spain, Trinidad, Oct., 1936.

COOLS-LARTIGUE, Alexander Raphael—B. 1899; ed. at St. Mary's Coll., St. Lucia, and Dominica Grammar Schl.; called to bar, Gray's Inn, 1924; admitted to bar, Leeward Is., 1924; practised at bar, 1924-35; ag. crown atty. and mag., dist. E, 1930.

COOMARASWAMY, Chinnappah.—B. 1887; ed. Hindu Coll., Jaffna, and Royal Coll., Colombo; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., April, 1910; extra office ast., Batticaloa kach., May, 1912; pol. mag., Matara, May, 1913; do., Puttalam, June, 1913; do., Chilaw, Feb., 1914; do., Point Pedro, June, 1915; eg. dist. judge, Batticaloa, Feb., 1918; ditto, Chilaw and Puttalam, Mar., 1920; addnl. ast. govt. agt., Chilaw and Puttalam, in addn., Aug., 1920; commr. of requests, Colombo, May, 1922; dep. comsnr., stamps, May, 1925; dist. judge, Kalutara, Apr., 1926; dep. comsnr., stamps, May, 1926; reglar., motor cars, Jan., 1928; ag. reglar.-gen., Sept., 1931; dist. judge, Kurunegala, June, 1932; do., Jaffna, Oct., 1933.

FLANAGAN, MAURICE JOSEPH, B.A. (Cantab.).—Asst. audr., S. Nigeria, Nov., 1912; audr., Cameroon Expedy. Force, 1916; audr., Windward Is., June, 1919; audr., Nyasaland, Oct., 1925; do., Uganda, 1935; do., Palestine, 1938.

FLECKER, ORIEL JOYCE, B.Sc.—Ed. Cheltenham Ladies' Coll.; assoc. of Cheltenham Ladies' Coll., 1908; gold med., Société Nationale des Professeurs de Français en Angleterre, 1909; B. Sc., Lond., 1912; Somerville Coll., Oxford, 1924-5; headmistress, girls' schl., Achimota, Gold Coast, 1925; author of "A School Chemistry," 1923.

FLEMING, ALAN MCKINSTERY, M.C., M.B., B.S. (Lond.), D.T.M. & H. (Eng.)—Served with 8th Bedfordshire Regt., B.E.F., 1915-18, ment. in desps.; Middlesex Hosp. Med. Schl.; house physician and house surg., Middlesex Hosp.; house physician, Brompton Hosp. for consumption; res. physician, Ruthin Castle; E. African med. serv., 1929; physician and lect. in medicine, Uganda Med. Schl., 1930-32; invalided, 1933; med. offr., Gibraltar, 1936.

FLEMING, EDWARD DONOVAN.—B. 1898; ed. Bradford Gram. Schl. and Jesus Coll., Camb.; 2nd lieut., R.G.A., Sept., 1917; Salonika, Dec., 1917-Feb., 1919; cadet, F.M.S., Apr., 1921, attd. Chinese prot., K. Lumpur; offr., cls. V, Apr., 1924; offr., cls. IV, Apr., 1928; asst. prot., Chinese, Taiping, May, 1930 and supt., convict estabt., in addn., Nov., 1930; offr., cls. III, Apr., 1933; prot., Chinese, Johore, July, 1934; do., Perak, Apr., 1936; do., Johore, Oct., 1937; ag. immigr. offr., S.S. and F.M.S., Mar., 1938.

FLEMING, ERNEST.—B. 1894; 5th class clk., crown agts. office, Oct., 1910; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd division of the civ. serv. and temporarily employed in the Bd. of Trade, Jan., 1912; assigned to C.O., April, 1912; on military service from 25th May, 1915 to 9th Feb., 1919; cler. offr., higher grade, 1st Apr., 1922; 2nd asst. acctnt., 22nd Oct., 1930.

FLEMMING, MAXWELL HECTOR VANDERMERE.—B. 1904; ed. Mill Hill Schl. and Walham Coll., Oxford; Sudan polit. serv., 1926-32; Grenoble Univ., France, 1933; lector in English, Univ. of Freiburg-im-Breisgau, Germany, 1934; senr. German mast., Merchiston Castle schl., Edinburgh, 1935-38; ch. inspr., schls., Cyprus, Sept., 1938.

FLEMING, W. P.—B. 1887; apptd. after compet. exam., S. and T. clk., G.P.O.; lent to C.O., 9th May, 1921; cler. offr., C.O., 1st Sept., 1921; on mil. serv., 4th Apr., 1916 to 4th May, 1919.

FLETCHER, SIR ARTHUR GEORGE MUNCHISON, K.C.M.G. (1930), KT. B.A.C.H. (1929), C.M.G. (1922), C.B.E. (1919).—Ed. Cheltenham Coll. and Trim. Coll., Oxford (exhib.); cadet, Hong Kong, 1901; seconded for famine relief work in Kwang Si. May-June, 1903; ag. asst. registr. gen., 1903; J.P., 1904; ag. asst. col. sec. and clk. of couns., 1905-8-9; priv. sec. to O.A.G., 1907; dep. offr. recvr., 1909; asst. to atty.-gen., 1909; registr., trade marks and letters patent, 1910; ag. assessor of rates, 1911; ag. dep. registr., 1911; priv. sec. to O.A.G., 1912; offr. recvr., 1912; ag. asst. col. sec. and clk. of couns., 1912; ag. treas., 1913; asst. col. sec. and clk. of couns., Aug., 1913; priv. sec. to O.A.G., and to gov., Aug.-Dec., 1913; ag. col. sec. and mem. of exec. and leg. couns. in 1916, 1917, 1918.
FAGAN, HENRY ALLAN.—B. 1889; ed. Victoria Coll., Stellenbosch and London Univ.; barrister-at-law, Middle Temple, 1909; advoc., Cape sup. ct., 1910; K.C., 1927; mem., Union Part., 1933; min. of educ., social welfare and native affrs., Union of S. Africa, 1938.

FAGAN, Hon. Mark, M.L.C.—B. 1873; ed. Waratah public schl., Tasmania; appd. mem., N.Z. leg. cncl., 1930; represented N.Z. at Empire Parly. Conf., London, 1935; leader, leg. cncl. and mem., exec. cncl., 1935.

FAHEY, FRANCOIS JOSEPH.—B. 1878; ed. St. Michael's Coll., Toronto, Canada; printer; arrived S. Africa, 1898; mem., prov. coun., Natal, 1920-23; prov. exec., 1924; joined bd. of trade and industries, Union of S. Africa, Oct., 1924; re-apptd., Apr., 1930; chmn., Mar., 1932.

FAIR, Hon. ARTHUR, LL.B. (N.Z.), K.C.—B. 1886; ed. state schls., Nelson Coll. and Victoria Univ. Coll., N.Z.; crown solr., 1921; prin. law offr., 1923; solr.-gen., 1925; judge, sup. ct., N.Z., 1934.

FAIRBAIRN, Sir GEORGE, KT. BACH. (1926).—B. 1855; ed. Geelong Grammar Schl. and Jesus Coll., Cambridge; M.L.A. for Toorak, Victoria, Oct., 1903 to Sept., 1906; M.H.R. for Fawkner, 1906-13; Commonwealth Senator for Victoria, May, 1917; agt.-gen. for Victoria, 1924-27.

FAIRBAIRN, H., M.D., Ch.B. (Glas.), D.T.M. & H. (Lond.)—B. 1898; mily. serv. 1917-19; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Jan., 1925; sleeping sickness offr., 1935.

FAIRCHILD, Joseph Bryant Wilson, B.Sc.—B. 1894; ed. Queen Elizabeth's Schl., Crediton and Bristol Univ.; ast. engr., P.W.D., F.M.S., May, 1923; ex. engr., May, 1932; ag. sr. ex. engr., Mar., 1936.

FAIRCLOUGH, F.R., M.B.E., (1938)—B. 1895; apptd. after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civil serv. and assigned to C.O., Aug., 1914; on military service from 13th Dec., 1915 to 9th March, 1919; priv. sec. to Sir James Stevenson, 12th Aug., 1922; cler. offr., higher grade, 7th July, 1923; staff offr., 15th July, 1933.

FAIRLEY, WILLIAM, B.A., A.M.I.C.E.—B. 1891; ed. St. Paul's Schl. and Magdalene Coll., Cambridge (schol.). B.A., (mech. science tripos) 1913; 6th Bn. E. FAIRWEATHER, James, N.D.A., U.D.A.—B. 1896; ed. Montrose Acad., Aberdeen Univ., N. of Soot. FALCONER, JOHN.—B. 1898; ed. Robert Gordon's Coll. and Aberdeen Univ.; M.A., Aberdeen (1st cls. hona.); cadet, F.M.S., Apr., 1921; passed cadet, July, 1922; ast. collr., land rev., K. FALLOWS, Lieut. Albert Edward, B.Sc. (Civ. Engnr.).—B. 1898; ed. Bolton Ch. Inst.Schl., Merohant Venturer's Coll. and Bristol Univ.; war serv., 1916-19; ast. engrnr., anti-malaria hr., F.M.S., Mar., 1924; ex. engrnr., Oct., 1933.

FANNIN, C. G., M.C., B.A. Oxon., Assoc. Inst. C. E.—B. 1890; ed. Hilton Coll., Natal, Rhodes schol., Exeter Coll., Oxford in 1908-11; hons. engrnr. sci., 1911; G. E. C. London, 1914; 1/1st Lond. Heavy Bty. R.G.A., 1915-16; adjt., 7th H. A. Group, 1917; (ment. in deeps, M.C.); ast. inspr., guns, Woolwich, 1918-19; Kenya survey dept., 1920; dist. survr., ast. land offr.; ch. survr., 1937; author of paper "Townplanning at Mombasa."

FANSHAWE, DENNY BASIL.—B. 1915; ed. Oundle Schol. and Pembroke Coll., Oxford, B.A. (forestry), 1936; ast. conserv., forests, Br. Guiana, Oct., 1937.

FARIS, Desmond William George, M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), M.B., B.S. (Lond.), D.P.H. (Lond.), Certif. L.S.T.M.—B. 1901; ed. Epson Coll., Lond. Hosp. Med. Coll., Lond. Univ.; med. offr., Malaya, Mar., 1926; ag. sr. health offr., Penang, July, 1935; do., S'pore, Feb., 1937.

FARQUHARSON, JAMES ROBBIE, B.Sc., A.M.Inst.C.E.—B. 1903; ed. Glasgow Univ. and Royal Tech. Coll., 1920-23; L.M.S. Rly., 1923-25; ast. engrnr., K.U.R. and H., 1925; senr. ast. engrnr. and acted frequently as dist. engrnr.; personal ast. to gen. man., Tanganyika Rly., May, 1937.

FARR, Frank James, M.B., Ch.B., L.D.S., D.M.R. & E.—B. 1900; radiologist, med. dept., Hong Kong, 1928.

FAULKNER, ODIN TOM, C.M.G. (1928).—B. 1890; ed. School of Trop. Agric., Trinidad (seconded), 1938.

FAULKNER, S.N.O.B.E. (1918)—Asts. auditor E.A.P., Jan., 1909; senr. asst. auditor, Apr., 1915; dep. ch. acctnt., Uganda Rly., 1917.

FAWCETT, CAPT. ARTHUR EDWARD, B.A., B.A.I. (Dublin), A.M.I.C.E., Chtd. Civ. Engnr.,—B. 1890; war. serv., 1916-19, R.K., France, Persia, Afghanistan, ment. in desp.; ast. engnr., F.M.S. Rlys., Apr., 1920; dist. engnr., Apr., 1926; do. grade I, Apr., 1929.

FAZAN, S. H., C.B.E. (1934), O.B.E. (1930), Ast. dist. commr., E. Africa Prot., Nov., 1911; dist. commr., Kenya, Feb., 1920; senr. dist. commr., 1934; prov. commr., 1936.

FEARON, FRANK ST. CLAIR.—Ed. FEATHERSTONE, ERIC KELLETT.—B. 1896; admstve. offr., cls. IV, Nigeria, 1921; cls. III, 1929; cls. II, 1937; ag. res., Aug.-Sept., 1937 and Mar.-June, 1938.

FEETHAM, RICHARD, C.M.G.—B. 1874; ed. FELTHAM, STANLEY CRATHERN, A.R.I.B.A., chtd. architect.—B. 1896; ed. Northern Polytechnic, London; architect, P.W.D., Hong Kong, 1923.

PENDALL, FRANCIS ALAN, L.S., N.Z. King's Coll. Auck. Univ.—B. 1891; lic. survr., N. Z., Mar., 1916; survr., F.M.S., Feb. 1920; do., Kedah, May, 1920; ast. supt., surveys, Sept., 1923; do., F.M.S., Mar., 1928; ast. ast. supt., surveys, S'pore, Dec., 1933; ag. senr. supt., do., Aug., 1936.

FENTON, JAMES STEVENSON, O.B.E. (1935).—B. 1891; ed. FERGUSON, HON. SIR DAVID GILBERT, KT. B.A. (1934).—B. 1861; called to the bar, 1890; judge of sup. ct., New S. Wales, Mar., 1912; ag. ch. just., 1929; rot., 1932.

FERGUSON, GORDON PATRICK, B.A. (Cambridge).—B. 1904; ast. mast., Hongkong educn. dept., 1929.

FITZGERALD, RICHARD DESMOND, B.A., M.D., B.Ch., B.A.O. (Dublin), T.C.D., D.T.M. and H. (Cantab.), certif. (hons.) L.S.T.M., M.C.—B. 1885; ed. ST. CLAIR-TOMPSON, GUY WARREN.—B. 1906; ed. Malvern and St. John's Coll., Cambridge, B.A. and dipl., forestry; forest botanist, teetse research dept., Tanganyika Territory, Aug., 1927; asst. conserv., forests, Gold Coast, Aug., 1934; do., Uganda, 1938.

ST. JOHNSTON, LIEUT.-COL. SIR REGINALD, K.C.M.G. (1931), C.M.G. (1923); Barrister-at-law (Middle Temple); M.R.C.S., L.R.C.P., Lond., etc.—Ed. Queen Elizabeth Coll., Guernsey and Cheltenham Coll.; various appts. in home civ. service; entered Fiji civ. serv., 1907; comsrr. Lau Islands, 1909; seconded for European war; D.A.D.M.S., B.E.F., France; subsequently attached to W.O. (brevet lieut.-col. and reed. thanks of S. of S.); col. sec., Falkland Is., Dec., 1918; ag. gov., Falkland Is., from Sept., 1919 to Apr., 1920; col. sec., Leeward Islds., Dec., 1919; ag. gov., Leeward Is., eight times; admstv. gov. of Antigua on many occasions; ag. admin., Dominica, 1926; admstv., St. Kitts-Nevis, 9th May, 1926; assumed duty, 23rd Nov., 1926; gov., Leeward Is., Sept., 1929; ret., 1935; author of "The Lau Islands, Fiji," "The Children of the Sun," "The Falkland Islands," "The Islanders of the Pacific," "South Sea Reminiscences," "West Indian Tales," "From a Colonial Governor's Notebook," "Strange Places and Strange People" and some novels, etc.

SALE, GILBERT NOEL, B.Sc. (Forestry, Edin.).—B. 1897; ed. King Alfred's Schl., Wantage, Edinburgh Univ. and Imp. Forestry Inst., Oxford; army serv., 1916-19; lieut., R.A. (S.R.); asst. conserv., forests, Cyprus, Mar., 1922; ag. asst. prin. forest offr., 1924; ag. prin. forest offr., 1926-28; dir., forests, Mauritius, Dec., 1928; conserv., forests, July, 1930; do., Palestine, 1935; do., grade F, 1936.

SALMON, FREDERICK JOHN, C.M.G. (1937), M.C., A.C.G.I., F.R.G.S., Lieut.-Col., R. of O., R.E.—B. 1882; ed. Univ. Coll. Schl., Lond., and Cent. Tech. Coll., S. Kensington; empd. on Transvaal Mines, 1904-1907; assoo., inst. of mining and metallurgy; asst. supt., surveys, Ceylon, June, 1908; supt., surveys, 1914; served with field survey units in France, 1915-19; thrice ment. in despatches; lieut.-col., supt., surveys, on staff (appl. surveys), Ceylon, 1924; ag. asst. surr.-gen., 1928; dir., land regist., and surveys, Cyprus, Sept., 1930; offr. cmdmg. sp. constab., 1932; dir., surveys, Palestine, 1933.

SALOMON, WALTER.—B. 1888; ed. St. Ignatius Coll. and Malta Univ.; elec. for 6th divn. in leg. assem., Oct., 1921; re-elec., June, 1924 and Aug., 1927; min. for industry and commerce, Aug., 1927.

SALTER, DAVID, Assoc. M.I.B.E.—B. 1893; served during the Great War, 1914-19; British mercantile marine, 1914-15; Royal Navy, 1915-19; tel. dept., Bahamas, 1920 (on contract); established, 1921; asst. supt., tels., 1928; supt., 1932.

SAMPSON, BASIL HERSEEN, M.C.—B. 1888; ed. St. Andrew's Coll., Grahamstown; M.B., B.S., Lond. Univ. (Guy's Hosp.), 1917; M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), 1915; temp. surg., R.N. (H.M.S. Benbow), 1915; tempy. capt., S.A.M.C., France, 1916; M.C., 1918; asst. bacteriologist, Guy's Hosp.; senr. govt. paish., Union of S. Africa health dept., Durban, 1931.

SAMUML, EDWIN HERBERT, B.A. Oxon (Balliol Coll.).—B. 1898; ed. SAMUEL, Rt. Hon. Sir HEBERT LOUIS, P.C. (1908), G.B.E. (1920), M.A.—B. 1870; ed.

Riding, Yorks., 1902-18; parly. under sec., home dept., 1905-9; chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster (with a seat in the cabinet), 1909-10 and 1915-16; P.M.G., 1910-14 and 1915-16; pres. of the L.G.B., 1914-15; sec. of state for home affairs, 1916; chmn. of the select comttee. of house of commons on national expenditure, 1917-18; British sp. commr. to Belgium, 1919; grand offr. of the Order of Leopold of Belgium, 1919; high commr., Palestine, 1920-26.

SANDERS, JOHN OWEN, M.I.T., A.M.L.C.E.—B. 1892; ed. SANDFORD, GEORGE RITCHIE, C.M.G.(1938), O.B.E. (1924), Barrister-at-Law, Inner Temple, 1924.—B. 1892; ed. Christ's Hosp. and Queens' Coll., Camb., B.A. and wrangler, 1914; asst. dist. commr., E. SANDFORD, THOMAS FREDERICK, C.M.G. (1935), M.B.E., B.A.—B. 1886; ed. Marlborough Coll. and Oriel Coll., Oxford; asst. native commr., N. Rhodesia, Sept., 1910; native commr., Apr., 1913; served in E. African campaign, 1915-19; ag. dist. commr., 1927; ag. prov. commr., in 1929, 1930 and 1931; prov. commr., Aug., 1932; temp. mem., leg. coun., 1932 and 1935; senr. prov. commr. and mem., exec. and leg. couns., 1936.

SANDY'S, MELVILL KEVENER TRELLAWNY, M.A. (Oxon.).—B. 1890; on mily. serv., Aug., 1914; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Nov., 1919; attd., Ratnapura kach., Nov., 1919; office asst. to govt. agt., N.W. SANKERALLI, ESAU JIMSHED, M.B., Ch.B., B.A.O. (Queen's University, Belfast), D.T.M. (Liverpool), L.M. (Dublin), D.P.H. (Belfast).—B. 1898; govt. med. offr., Trinidad, 1923; asst. res. surg., col. hosp., 1929; junr. med. inspr., health, Aug., 1935; M.O.H., S.W. dist., Jan., 1936.

SANSON, CHARLES HENRY, C.M.G. (1938)—B. 1886; ed. SARAVANAMUTTU, PAIKIASOTHY.—B. 1894; B.A., Lond.; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Aug., 1919; attd., Colombo, kach., Aug., 1919; attd. to Matale Kaoh., June, 1920; addnl. dist. judge, Badulla, Mar., 1921; pol. mag., Dandagamuwa, Sept., 1921; ditto, Kurunegala, June, 1922; addnl. asst. govt. agt., Colombo, Mar., 1923; addnl. asst. dir., educ., Dec., 1925; asst. govt. agt., Mullaitivu, Dec., 1926; dist. judge, Kegalle, Mar., 1929; dist. judge, Kalutara, Apr., 1932; asst. govt. agt., Kalutara, Apr., 1933; rubber contr., May, 1934; tea contr. in addn., Apr., 1935.

ARGEANT, CAPT. R. G., M.B.E. (1928), A.I.N.A., F.R.G.S.—Port offr., Kenya, Jan., 1917; port capt., K.U.R. & H., 1925.

SAUNDERS, MAJOR ALAN, O.B.E. (1932), M.C.(1917).—B. 1886; ed. Christ's Hosp.; Indian pol., 1906-14; Great War, 1914-20; France, Flanders, Palestine; wounded twice; three times ment. in despe.; dep. inspir. genl., Palestine pol., 1926; King's pol. med., Sept., 1929; commr., Nigeria pol., 1936; inspir.-gen., pol. and prisons, Palestine, Nov., 1937.

SAUNDERS, GODFREY ESTRIDGE.—B. 1884; offr. of cust., Cape Town, 1901; 1st grade examnt., Mossel Bay, 1915; prin. clk., Pretoria, 1923; senr. inspir., Johannesburg, 1931; surv., cust., Port Elizabeth, 1933; investigation offr., London, 1933; ch. inspir., Pretoria, 1936; asst. dep. commr., Pretoria, 1937; dep. commr., 1938.

SAUVÉ, HON. ARTHUR, P.C. (Can.).—B. 1875; ed. Seminary of Ste. SAWARD, CAPT. SIDNEY CARMON, M.C. (1916), M.M. (1916).—B. 1889; fellow of surveyors' inst.; served with 509 (1-1) Lond. Field Coy., R.E., 6th divn.; home serv., Aug. to Dec., 1914; France and Germany, Dec., 1914 to June, 1919; Ireland, June to Aug., 1919; commdg., cadre, 12th Field Co., R.E.; commd., Sept., 1915; lieut., June, 1916; capt., Oct., 1918; ag. major, Dec., 1918 to Jan., 1919; ment. in desps., Mar., 1919; survr., Gold Coast, Nov., 1919; field supervisor Apr., 1924; ag. dep. survr.-gen. on various occasions, 1926-32; ag. survr.-gen., Feb.-June, 1927; asst. survr.-gen., Apr., 1929; ag. survr.-gen., Mar.-Aug., 1934, and Mar.-Aug., 1936; dir. of surveys, 1938.

SAXTON, SIDNEY WARING.—Ed. Toulouse (France), and Dean Close Sch., Cheltenham; paymr. cadet, R.N., July, 1906; paymr.-lieut. comdr., Mar., 1918; 1st cls. Navy, 1920; passed Tropical African service course (all subjects, 2nd part); barrister-at-law, Middle Temple, 1925; promoted pay commdr., ret. list, 1927; dep. prov. comanr., 1930; prov. comanr., 1938.

SAYERS, ELDER FRANK.—B. 1889; ed. King's Coll. Sch., Wimbledon, St. John's Coll., Cambridge, and Grenoble Univ., B.A., LL.B. (Cantab.); barrister-at-law (Inner Temple), Apr., 1913; passed lower and higher stand. exams. in Tonno, and lower stand. exam. in Koranko; war service, E. Africa, 1918; asst. dist. comanr., Sierra Leone, Jan., 1915; dist. comanr., Aug., 1922.

SAYERS, GERALD FLEMING.—B. 1893; ed. Westminster and Christ Church, Oxford; B.A. (hon.) 1914; asst. dist. comanr., E. SCAMMELL, ERNEST HENRY.—B. 1873; ed. privately; sec. various business concerns, 1891-1907; visited Australia, engaged in business and journalism in Canada, 1907-1913; organizing sec., Canadian Peace Centenary Association, under the auspices of the govt. of Canada, 1913; asst. cable censor, dept. of militia and defence, Canada, 1915; sec., mil. hosps. comanr., Canada, 1915; asst. dep. min. and sec., dept. of soldiers' civil re-estabmt., Canada, 1918; negotiated reciprocal agreements between Canadian, British and United States Govts., regarding treatment and training of Naval and Military Forces resident in these countries, 1919; sec., pensions divn., dept. of pensions and national health, 1931; Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Secretaries (London); Fellow of the Royal Colonial Institute (London); mem. of the Exec. of the Canadian Peace Centenary Assoc.

SCHARFF, JOHN WILLIAM, B.A., M.D., B.A.O., B.Ch., D.P.H. (T.C.D.), D.T.M. & H. SCHERMBRI, JUDGE SALVATORE, LL.D.—B. 1881; matric., Malta Univ., 1899; LL.D., 1907; ag. judge, Malta, 1936; judge, 1937.

SCHMIDT, CARL FRIEDRICH, B.A.—Civ. serv. law olk., law dept., Cape, May, 1893; control and audit office, July, 1893; asst. examnr. of accts., Jan., 1894; examnr., May, 1898; ch. examnr., July, 1907; inspr. of accts., Jan., 1909; prin. olk., Apr., 1912; sec. educn. dept., Bloemfontein, 16th Aug., 1915; ag. dir. of educn., O.F.S., July, 1918; dir. of educn., O.F.S., June, 1920; sec. for interior, Sept., 1926; contr. and audr.-gen., 1929; rector, Pretoria univ., 1935.

SCHOLEFIELD, WILLIAM.—Dep. olk., res. mag.s. ct., Jamaica, Mar., 1913; olk., res. mag.s. ct., Feb., 1917; asst. comanr. and mag., Turks and Caicos Islands, July, 1919; ag. comanr.,

SHUTE, GEOFFREY GAY, C.M.G. (1939), B.A. (Cantab.).—B. 1892; ed. St. Andrew's Sch., Eastbourne, Uppingham and Clare Coll., Cambridge; ast. dist. offr., Nigeria, 1915; cl. SIDEBOOTHAM, JOHN BIDDULPH, B.A. (1914), M.A. (1920).—B. 1891; ed. (Sir J. Maffey) to W. Indies, 1936.

SIDLEY, WILLIAM HENRY FRANCIS, B.A. (Trinity Coll., Dublin).—Cadet, R.I.C., Aug., 1908; 3rd cls. dist. inspr., Oct., 1908; 2nd cls., Feb., 1910; 1st cls., Aug., 1919; counsr., Nov., 1920; served in R.I.C. until disbandment of that force, July, 1922; depot inspr. SINEL, ROY, A.R.A.N.Z.—Ed. Auckland Gram.
